teams.heading: Vilimoni Botitu starts late as Isikeli Rabitu is reportedly sick
teams.body: Fiji changed their starting XV late, with Vilimoni Botitu coming in after Isikeli Rabitu was reportedly sick. Botitu spilled the ball inside his own 22, and France's Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang secured the attacking bonus point before half-time, the hosts leading 26-3 at the break. Coach Jake White's side, which started with 10 France-based players, got tries from Vinaya Habosi and Selestino Ravutaumada, but the 54-17 defeat was a fourth straight loss in the inaugural Nations Championship.

lead.why: A new report with a Fiji-specific team change, a late starting-XV switch when Isikeli Rabitu was reportedly sick.

teams.heading: Henry Pollock scores twice as England beat Australia 45-22 at Twickenham
teams.body: Henry Pollock's two tries, in the 55th and 58th minutes, came three minutes apart and turned a 19-10 half-time lead into a rout. The win came amid reports of a rift between Steve Borthwick and his players, a report England's hooker Jamie George called shocking. Ollie Chessum also crossed, and Henry Slade was named player of the match.

teams.heading: Galthié recalls Julien Marchand, Gaël Fickou and Teddy Thomas for Springboks test
teams.body: Romain Ntamack's shoulder injury has forced a fly-half reshuffle, and Galthié has turned to experience for the Paris test. Hooker Julien Marchand, sidelined since a thigh injury in early October, returned for Toulouse on Saturday and could go straight into the starting XV. Centre Gaël Fickou, 32, and winger Teddy Thomas, 33, are back in the group, along with flyhalf Louis Carbonel, who has not featured in a France matchday 23 since 2022.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan fails head injury assessment as Robert Baloucoune also goes off
teams.body: Ireland's injury list from the Argentina win is a lengthy one. Captain Dan Sheehan, deputising for the injured Caelan Doris, was forced off in the first half after failing a head injury assessment, though Farrell said he "seems fine in the dressing room". Robert Baloucoune also went off with a knock in the 58th minute, Sean Jansen took a "bang" to his knee, and Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns. The knocks are particularly concerning after the performance of Farrell's back three.

teams.heading: Quesada to name Italy's Argentina team in Thursday press release
teams.body: Italy's team for the Argentina test in Genoa will be announced in a press release on Thursday, with Gonzalo Quesada also holding a Zoom press conference that day, the federation has confirmed. The Azzurri then hold a captain's run at the Stadio Ferraris on Friday, open to media for its first 15 minutes, before Saturday's second test of the November window. The schedule then runs on to Fiji in Udine on 21 November before the final weekend at Twickenham.

teams.heading: Ewan Ashman scores hat-trick in Scotland's 21-43 defeat by All Blacks
teams.body: Ewan Ashman's three first-half tries, on 8, 27 and 38 minutes, left Scotland trailing 21-24 at the break against the All Blacks. Scotland then failed to score after the interval, and New Zealand added 19 unanswered points on their way to a 43-21 win at Murrayfield. It was Scotland's 10th defeat in their last 11 meetings with New Zealand, and the wait for a first win over them goes on.

teams.heading: Dewi Lake says Wales let themselves down in Japan win
teams.body: Captain Dewi Lake was frustrated despite the bonus-point win. "There were massive parts of that game where we let ourselves down," he said, adding that the group had promised in camp to do things it probably did not manage against Japan. Josh Adams scored twice, with Archie Griffin and Louis Rees-Zammit also crossing, as Wales took the bonus point in their 28-21 win in Cardiff. Lake said the victory still mattered: "A win is massive for this group." Wales now face New Zealand on Saturday.

teams.heading: Pumas prospect Marcos Camerlinckx signs for Bath, leaving Argentina at 22
teams.body: Bath have announced the signing of uncapped prop Marcos Camerlinckx, his first professional experience outside South America. The 22-year-old joins a front row that includes Will Stuart, Archie Griffin and Kieran Verden, and he has not yet played for Los Pumas. He recently played for the Argentina XV against the USA in Fort Lauderdale and was a Super Rugby Americas champion with Los Pampas. His father, Pablo Camerlinckx, was a No. 8 for Los Pumas, earning his final cap against Wales in 1999.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the pack about Argentina itself; the other fresh pieces cover Italy and Ireland.

teams.heading: Wallabies fall 45-22 at Twickenham despite Max Jorgensen's halftime intercept try
teams.body: Max Jorgensen's intercept try, scored as the clock went red, pulled the Wallabies back to 19-10 behind at halftime. Henry Pollock, a makeshift winger, scored a double after being introduced on the wing, and England's four second-half tries sealed the 45-22 win. Captain Harry Wilson was blunt at full time about the Wallabies' slow start. The bench made significant inroads in the second half, with Filipo Daugunu, Rob Valetini, Taniela Tupou and Ben Donaldson of note.

lead.why: It is a new match review from the Australian side's perspective, covering the Wallabies' latest result against England.

teams.heading: Kenta Fukuda's late try falls short as Japan lose 28-21 in Cardiff
teams.body: Japan trailed only 21-14 at half-time after Ben Gunter and captain Warner Dearns crossed, with Naoto Saito converting both. Josh Adams scored twice for Wales, and Louis Rees-Zammit also crossed before the break. Replacement scrum-half Kenta Fukuda's late try, from a passing move involving several team-mates, and Shinya Komura's conversion cut the margin to seven before Wales held on.

teams.heading: Two All Blacks could miss Wales clash after injury concerns
teams.body: Two New Zealand players are reported to be at risk of missing the Test against Wales after picking up injuries. The All Blacks have won all four of their Nations Championship matches, most recently beating Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield on Saturday, and carry a points difference of +73 into the Wales fixture. Wales is the Round five opponent, and New Zealand go there unbeaten in the competition so far.

teams.heading: Pieter-Steph du Toit quits Japan as Boks return home on pay cuts
teams.body: Pieter-Steph du Toit announced on Friday that he is leaving Toyota Verblitz to join Malcolm Marx, Kwagga Smith and Manie Libbok in returning to South Africa. Rapport's sources say most returning Boks are taking an average salary cut of at least 50%, because no South African team can match Japanese offers. One player was reportedly earning about R18-million a year in Japan and is now on about R6.5-million with his South African team, including SA Rugby's Poni contribution. Cheslin Kolbe rejoined the Stormers this season from Tokyo Suntory Sungoliath.

lead.why: A new, South Africa-focused story on Springboks returning from Japan on pay cuts, with a named player's departure.
